Probability the disclosures are gross rather than IT power; the notebook's section 8 sweeps this. Lowered 0.2 -> 0.1 on 7/30/26 (per Josh): the definitional ambiguity was making OpenAI's CI nearly as wide as Anthropic's despite OpenAI's far harder power anchor

Accuracy of OpenAI's internal total-power figure, aside from rounding and the IT-vs-gross definition. Undercounted providers (Azure/Oracle/CoreWeave) or newly-online capacity push the true figure above the disclosure; overstatement pushes below. Median ~1.04, a mild upward lean
Half-step of the disclosures' 0.1 GW rounding: the true figure sits within +/-50 MW of each disclosed power number. Sampled as a triangular peaked at 0, independent per year

End-2025 IT power, 90% CI 1.0-1.9 GW (geomean ~1.38, close to the memo's 1.4 GW). Widened from 1.09-1.8 on 7/30/26 (per Josh): the old cap sat just under OpenAI's 1.9 GW point figure, but OpenAI's own power carries sampled uncertainty (definition/accuracy/rounding), so Anthropic at 1.9 is consistent with 'OpenAI ahead' - that world just implies an even larger OpenAI (correlation not modeled directly)

Trainium2 share of end-2025 IT power, anchored on site power in Epoch's data-center directory: New Carlisle ~626 MW at end-2025 (possibly still ~400 MW) + Madison MS ~284 MW (unclear if all Anthropic's) + residual Trainium2 elsewhere. High anchor ~1.0 GW of 1.4 GW (~70%; also near a prior ceiling given Anthropic's Nvidia and TPU use); low anchor ~500 MW (~35%). Was (0.4, 0.8) chip-count-anchored before 7/3/26

Sampled efficiency multiplier on the non-Trainium (Nvidia + TPU) H100e-per-MW bucket, whose specs are otherwise borrowed as point values. Mirrors the OpenAI model's sampled fleet-efficiency spread (deployment lag + nvidia_it_overhead put its H100e/MW at 0.83x-1.16x of median, p95/p5 1.39x), widened to 0.8-1.25 (1.56x) for the extra TPU-side uncertainty (TDP-derived IT power with a const overhead, generation mix from sales data). Geomean 1.0 leaves the median untouched. Added 8/4/26 per Josh

Sampled efficiency multiplier on the Trainium2 H100e-per-MW bucket, collapsing the chip's power uncertainty into one parameter. The point value comes from Epoch's Frontier Data Centers methodology: per-chip IT power = ~500 W TDP (a SemiAnalysis estimate - AWS publishes no TDP) x a 1.74 combined server+IT overhead borrowed from the Nvidia GB200 NVL72 reference design = ~870 W, which is exactly what the New Carlisle 300k-H100e/398-MW equivalency backs out. Both factors are uncertain: SemiAnalysis's own rack estimates imply 750-845 W all-in per chip (overhead 1.5-1.69x, giving a ~1.05-1.16 upside on efficiency), while a hotter TDP or overhead pushes the other way (~0.85). Geomean ~1.01, so the median barely moves. Added 8/4/26 per Josh

Anthropic's 2024 full-year cloud compute spend, around The Information's reported $2.5B (90% CI +/-20% for reporting/definition error; widened from +/-12% on 7/30/26 per Josh). Correlated 0.5 with cloud_spend_2025 in code (same reporting). Input to the end-2024 backcast (model_anthropic_2024)

Anthropic's 2025 full-year cloud compute spend, around The Information's reported $6.8B (90% CI ~ +/-20%, geomean ~6.8; widened from +/-12% on 7/30/26 per Josh). Correlated 0.5 with cloud_spend_2024 in code. Input to the end-2024 backcast

Within-2025 spend growth as a multiple of the average 2024->2025 growth (~2.7x/yr): 1 = one smooth exponential through both annual totals; <1 front-loaded; >1 back-loaded. Leans back-loaded and is narrower than pure ignorance (was to(0.6,1.6) before 7/16/26): SemiAnalysis's quarterly Anthropic build hugs the smooth curve through 2024 then runs ~1.3 through 2025, and the WSJ Q1-26 compute+infra figure ($3.4B/qtr ~ $13.6B/yr) lands between the fitted end-2025 rate and SA's steeper Q1-26 build. Sets the end-2024 spending rate in the backcast

Anthropic's effective 2024 price per H100e-hour, billed around the clock. SemiAnalysis's 1-yr H100 contract index runs ~$3/hr through 2023 falling to the low-$2s through 2024; Anthropic's effective rate sits below that curve (multi-year terms, scale and pricing power with closely tied clouds, the TPU v5e slice entering the mix) but can sit above pure GPU-hour pricing since 'compute spend' plausibly includes auxiliary costs (storage, networking, CPU fleets). Divides the end-2024 spending rate in the backcast

Share of Colossus 1 phase 2 (the second 100k Hoppers, completing the 150k H100 + 50k H200 configuration) online at Dec 31 2024, on top of the firm 100k phase 1 (online Sept 2024). Linear interpolation between Epoch's Sept 2024 and Feb 2025 milestones says 71%; xAI's December 'doubling complete' announcement says 100% (Epoch didn't credit it); a back-loaded H200 arrival pulls it down. Left end tightened 0.30 -> 0.40 on 9/1/26 (per Josh) so the mean (~0.68) sits at the linear interpolation. Replaces capacity_accuracy_2024

Probability that ANY of Colossus 2 cluster 2 (the S-1's 110k GB300s, ~278k H100e, Epoch-dated Apr 6 2026) was energized by Dec 31 2025, on top of the disclosure-pinned 554k floor (C1 276k + C2 cluster 1 278k). Epoch's Jan 13 satellite read shows the cluster's cooling still under construction, so the central case is nothing live (median share 0); the Q2-26 earnings deck (1.0 GW at Mar 31, implying a ~mid-Feb finish) keeps a partial-energization tail open. Mixed in code with c2_cluster2_share_if_live_2025: share = 0 with prob 1-p, else the share-if-live draw. Per Josh 9/1/26 (0.35 -> 0.33 same day); replaces the 0.43 point estimate and, before that, capacity_accuracy_2025

Share of Colossus 2 cluster 2 online at Dec 31 2025 GIVEN that some of it was (see c2_cluster2_any_live_2025). Centered on the linear ramp from cluster 1's Oct 19 2025 start to Epoch's Apr 6 2026 completion date: 73/169 days = 0.43 median. 90% CI 0.20-0.66 spans a slow start through the ~62% the Q2-26 earnings deck implies (1.0 GW at Mar 31 -> ~mid-Feb finish). Was norm(0, 0.40), median 0.20; re-centered on the interpolation per Josh 9/1/26. Overall share: P5 = median = 0, mean ~0.14, P95 ~0.55

Non-Colossus cloud compute at end-2024: the Oracle Grok-2 cluster (20k H100s, ~$340M/yr at $2/hr) anchors the floor. S-1 p.117 puts 2024 AI R&D spend at $1.176B, which also covers X R&D, staff/data, and ~$300M of Colossus 1 depreciation, so the cloud bill was likely a $300M-$1B/yr run rate = roughly 20-60k H100e. Per the frontier hub methodology doc (Aug 2026); was to(10k,60k) incl. small owned sites

Non-Colossus cloud compute at end-2025: S-1 p.112 increases (infra+cloud R&D +$1.44B, infra+cloud cost of revenue +$412M, vs GPU depreciation +$1.673B booked separately - so much of the ~$1.8B is non-GPU infrastructure) on the $300M-$1B 2024 baseline imply a $1-2B/yr spend rate, hard ceiling ~$3B = ~57-114k H100e at $2/hr. Per the frontier hub methodology doc (Aug 2026); was to(40k,150k)
